questions.question: The formation energy per atom of a compound is …

options.b: (E_tot − Σ n_i μ_i⁰) / Σ n_i with elemental reference energies μ_i⁰

questions.explanation: Energy relative to the elements in their reference states, per atom.

questions.question: A phase with E_hull = 0 …

options.a: is on the convex hull (thermodynamically stable at 0 K)

questions.explanation: E_hull = 0 means no combination of other phases has lower energy at that composition.

questions.question: The convex hull is constructed from …

options.b: the lower convex envelope of (composition, E_f) points

questions.explanation: Lower convex hull in composition–energy space (Qhull in pymatgen).

questions.question: For a metastable phase, E_hull is …

options.b: the energy per atom released by decomposing into the hull phases at the same composition

questions.explanation: It is a thermodynamic driving force, not a kinetic barrier.

questions.question: Why does SymPhase refuse to build a hull when an element has no reference entry?

options.b: formation energies and the simplex corners require the elemental references

questions.explanation: Every element must have at least one pure-element calculation to define μ_i⁰ and the hull corners.

questions.question: Can you put Materials Project energies and your own VASP energies into one hull?

options.b: only if computed with identical settings (functional, PAW, U, corrections …)
options.d: yes, if ENCUT is the same

questions.explanation: Total energies are only comparable for identical computational settings; MP uses its own correction scheme (MP2020).

questions.question: Which statement about E_hull and synthesizability is most accurate?

options.b: many metastable phases with E_hull of a few tens of meV/atom are made; there is no universal cut-off

questions.explanation: Kinetics, entropy and finite temperature matter; typical screening windows are 25–100 meV/atom.

questions.question: The stability margin (equilibrium reaction energy) of a stable phase is …

options.b: how far it lies below the hull formed by all OTHER phases (negative = robust)

questions.explanation: Removing the phase and recomputing the hull gives the energy it gains relative to its neighbours.

questions.question: Hands-on: load examples/hull/NiAl_binary.csv. How many entries are stable (elements included)?
questions.explanation: Ni, Al, Ni3Al, NiAl, Ni2Al3 and NiAl3 (toy data).

questions.question: Hands-on (Ni–Al): E_hull of 'Ni5Al3-Pt5Ga3' in meV/atom?
questions.explanation: It decomposes into 1/2 Ni3Al + 1/2 NiAl, 42.5 meV/atom higher.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ni–Al): 'NiAl2-hyp' decomposes into …
questions.explanation: 0.556 Ni2Al3 + 0.444 NiAl3: the two hull phases bracketing x(Ni)=1/3.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ni–Al): E_hull of the L1₀ polymorph 'NiAl-L10' (meV/atom)?
questions.explanation: A polymorph decomposes into the ground state of the same composition: −0.540 − (−0.665) = 125 meV/atom.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ti–Ni–Sn): stability margin of half-Heusler TiNiSn in meV/atom?
questions.explanation: −97.4 meV/atom: removing TiNiSn from the hull would raise the energy at its composition by that amount.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ti–Ni–Sn): 'TiNiSn2-hyp' decomposes into …
questions.explanation: 0.75 TiNiSn + 0.25 Sn, E_hull = 127.5 meV/atom.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ti–Zr–Ni–Sn): E_hull of the (Ti0.5Zr0.5)NiSn SQS in meV/atom?
questions.explanation: 5 meV/atom above the TiNiSn + ZrNiSn tie-line: a small positive mixing energy.

questions.question: Experimentally (Ti,Zr)NiSn solid solutions exist although the SQS lies above the hull. The main reason is …

options.b: configurational entropy −TΔS_mix lowers the free energy at synthesis temperatures

questions.explanation: A few meV/atom of mixing enthalpy is easily overcome by ideal mixing entropy at 1000 K (next question).

questions.question: Ideal mixing on ONE sublattice per formula unit of (Ti0.5Zr0.5)NiSn (3 atoms). What is T·S_mix at 1000 K in meV per atom?
questions.hint: S_mix = k_B ln 2 per mixing site; k_B = 8.617e-5 eV/K
questions.explanation: k_B·1000 K·ln2 = 59.7 meV per mixing site = 19.9 meV/atom ≫ 5 meV/atom mixing enthalpy.

questions.question: Hands-on (Ti–Zr–Hf–Ni–Sn): the high-entropy (TiZrHf)NiSn SQS decomposes into …
questions.explanation: 2/3 (Zr0.5Hf0.5)NiSn + 1/3 TiNiSn, E_hull ≈ 2.7 meV/atom: in the toy data (Zr,Hf)NiSn is itself on the hull.

questions.question: How does SymPhase visualise systems with more than four elements?

options.b: grids of all binary/ternary sub-system hulls, E_hull bar charts and pseudo-binary slices

questions.explanation: plot_subsystems, plot_ehull_bar and plot_pseudo_binary work for any number of elements.

questions.question: What does `symphase hull -n 40` (or MPI) parallelise?

options.c: per-entry E_hull/decompositions/margins, candidate screening, VASP-folder parsing and pseudo-binary hull points

questions.explanation: The hull construction (Qhull) is serial and fast; everything done per entry or per candidate is distributed over processes (one node) or MPI ranks (many nodes).
